description.p: Shopping List keeps what the household needs to buy. Every item has one of three priorities and a category, so the list is easy to scan in the shop.

It works offline. The list stays on your device unless the household shares a space over storage it configured itself, on GitHub or on a WebDAV server of its choice. There is no server of ours, no account and no telemetry.

screenshot.caption: The shopping list, sorted by when it is needed
The shopping list, sorted by when it is needed

ul.li: The preferences can create a space, kept in step through a GitHub repository or a WebDAV folder, and leave a space after a confirmation that says what is deleted on this device and what stays in the storage.
Report a Problem… in the main menu sends a problem or an idea as a GitHub issue, with your own token or through the filled-in issue form in the browser; About links to that form.

Lists with text fields scroll on a phone: a touch that starts a drag on a field, such as a category name, no longer focuses the field and opens the keyboard; a tap still edits it, and a mouse works as before. Checked in GTK's Broadway backend, which has no on-screen keyboard: the check is that the drag focused no field, not how far the list moved.
The KitchenOwl server address is no longer refused as "no web address" in the Linux app.
The list can be kept in step with a list on your KitchenOwl server, in both directions.
The app's page in the software centre shows screenshots.
The sync status and the space on this device are now worded as in the other household apps.
The list syncs when you open the app and after a change instead of every few seconds; pull the list down or choose Sync now to sync at any time, and turn automatic syncing off in the preferences.

description.p: Shopping List is now also an app for Linux phones and desktops.
